reviewer: library_queue (independent of the original gameplay implementation)
scope: Remaining source adapter, Tower rider leases, roller visual broadphase and delayed Slosher angle reuse.
result: Three callback/custom-input regressions fixed; soft-push invariant hoist removed and rejected after a native collision-callback counterexample. No additional regression found in the reviewed rider lease or finite roller broadphase.

findings.counterexample: The AddSpawnSpeedYRateByXZ getter changed the delayed projectile yaw from 0 to PI/2 between the second and third velocity arguments. The original final cosine read saw the new yaw; the once-at-start cache check did not.
findings.resolution: The ready flag is reused, but every sine/cosine site reads and validates its live angle at the original expression position using Object.is against the cached angle. Parameter, angle and muzzle mutation and throwing getters retain original read/call/exception order.
findings.validation: 64 extracted-production-function comparisons, including cache enabled/disabled, signed zero, NaN/Infinity, changing yaw/pitch, muzzle/parameter mutation, thrown getters and thrown packet callback.

findings.counterexample: A spawn callback changed shared normal scratch _v3 to (1,0,0). Subsequent particles used the new normal with stale tangent basis scalars.
findings.resolution: Basis is created lazily after the original two RNG draws. It is recomputed when any normal component changes by Object.is; stable normals reuse copied tangent scalars. Recursive burst calls, tangent scratch clobbering and RNG-induced normal changes retain birth order, attributes and draw counts.
findings.validation: 120 seeded actual-burst comparisons across tangent mutation, normal mutation, recursive burst, RNG normal mutation, throwing spawn callback and throwing RNG.

findings.counterexample: An Actor custom distanceTo admitted a target near the camera whose geometric distance from the actor exceeded the ordinary radius. The new component rejection skipped that target before consulting the custom metric.
findings.resolution: Keep only the axis bound on the private native camera vector _v before its length calculation. Actor distance is the unchanged original if (a.pos.distanceTo(e.pos) > maxR) continue expression, preserving its exact getter lookup, receiver, call and exception semantics. No actor-component bound, argument array or generic call helper is introduced.
findings.validation: Four real assist-function comparisons for near/far custom metrics and throwing lookup/call preserve exact property order, receiver, LOS trace and result; the existing 30/60/120 Hz target-transition and boundary-distance parity test also passes.
findings.buildConstraint: The prior Function.prototype.call.call fallback legitimately triggered the existing orphan scanner Function-identifier gate and retained an otherwise unnecessary charge-hit-cue module. The scanner gate was not changed; the optimization was narrowed to the private camera vector.

findings.counterexample: The native softPushActor invoked physics.bodyFits, which synchronously replaced actors[0]. The original next pair reread the roster slot, while the hoisted actor kept pushing the removed actor. Hoisting PLAYER.radius across the same callbacks similarly loses live radius changes.
findings.resolution: Removed all three soft-push source transform anchors and restored original per-pair Actor and radius reads. Retaining live reads would leave only two multiplications to cache at the cost of extra comparisons/branches, so this proposal is not adopted.
findings.validation: Four comparisons of the actual native softPushActor and extracted base/current pair loop under roster replacement, radius mutation, both mutations, and a throwing collision callback.

areasWithoutAdditionalFindings.reason: Depth increments before the synchronous collector/consumer, each depth owns separate arrays and rows, public collector calls stay fresh, instance-overridden collectors avoid pooling, and finally clears retained actor references and restores depth. Existing executed public-snapshot and exception test passed.

areasWithoutAdditionalFindings.area: roller finite component bound and occupied slot traversal
areasWithoutAdditionalFindings.reason: The bound rejects only finite separations with a component strictly above radius*3 and keeps the exact hypot boundary test otherwise. Reversing delta signs preserves hypot; no actor collision/paint state is touched. Occupancy-bit traversal retains ascending slot order and only initialized slot heads are read.

validation.finalScope: Aim Assist camera-vector-only bound after final-build orphan-scanner review; both review 4/4 and existing parity 9/9 rerun successfully.

audioReadOnlyFollowup.finding: The remote audio idle guard cannot skip an actor with wr.rolling or an existing roll handle. The composed remote volume expression is unchanged. The timeout receipt has an admitted playing+registered real loop but zero owner velocity, so zero gain follows that expression. The owner ends at x=-1.9501 from supported x=-1.9, opposite the verified +X corridor; the UI owner is collecting the bounded pulse/position/input/wire timeline. No audio-source change or gate relaxation was made by this review.
audioReadOnlyFollowup.sourceExplanation: The existing rolling movement path sets velocity along current actor.yaw and uses input magnitude, while the desired move heading is approached by Actor._face after movement through a rate/acceleration-limited spring. The harness resets body yaw to -PI/2 (-X), then KeyS requests +X for 250 ms: the initial -X travel is expected during that reversal. place() also leaves yawVel and _faceTarget from the previous motion. The first successful pulse moved toward -X as well (x=-2.2401 from -1.9), consistent with that mechanism. Browser diagnostics are still required to attribute the missed positive audio window definitively; no production/audio/gate changes were made here.

limitations: These are source/function and Three.js regressions, not a new hardware performance or real multiplayer certification. The browser audio gate remains owned by the UI agent.
